solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Forest dwellers like returning with food

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: as means like, in 'as good as gold'
kai is a New Zealand word for food

explanation.surface: Woodland folk who, like it or not, come home to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: KAI, a Maori-derived word for food, is common in Azed-style barred puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sakai are an aboriginal people of the Malay peninsula's forests, so they are literally forest dwellers.

clue.text: Indian captain, alight, hoisted a run

indicators.note: hoisted means lifted, and in a down answer lifting reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: to debus is to get off a bus, to alight
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An Indian team captain, fired up, lofts a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alight' looks like an adjective meaning on fire; here it is the verb to get off a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A subedar was an Indian officer in the British Indian army, ranking roughly with a captain.

clue.text: Something to entertain the children? I had five in small tub

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a kid is a small wooden tub
I'd is the contraction of I had
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Bathtime fun: five little ones squeezed into a small tub.
explanation.walkthrough: A kid in this sense is an old word for a small wooden vessel, not a child, though the surface wants children.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidvid is slang for children's television or video, made to keep the young amused.

clue.text: Very uptight about strong drink — it's related to chest pain

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another

blocks.note: anal means obsessively tense and fussy
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A tense drinker's spirits bring on chest pains.
explanation.walkthrough: Anal in its psychological slang sense means extremely uptight, so 'Very uptight' is one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Anginal is the adjective from angina, the heart condition marked by pain in the chest.

clue.text: Article with end cut Times garbled

indicators.note: cutting the end lops off the last letter
garbled means scrambled, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper article in The Times, cut short and garbled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a newspaper piece; both the article and The Times are wordplay red herrings for each other.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article in a list or a newspaper piece.

clue.text: It casts a glow right inside a heap

indicators.note: being inside means sitting within another word, which wraps around it

blocks.note: taken as written
a clamp is a stacked heap, as of bricks or potatoes
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Something glowing found buried within a pile.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes after the C of CLAMP, and A stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces brilliant light from an electric arc, so it is a lamp that casts a glow.

clue.text: E.g. CRI's die horribly (or did, mostly)

definitions.text: E.g. CRI's die horribly (or did, mostly)

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Charles I's killers came to a horrible end, most of them.
explanation.walkthrough: CR I is Carolus Rex I, Charles I; many who signed his death warrant were later executed, so the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Regicides are king-killers, and Charles I's judges are history's best-known example.

clue.text: Lily having term absent

blocks.note: to call something is to term it
A is a register abbreviation for absent

explanation.surface: A girl named Lily is away for the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' looks like a school period but is the verb to name.
explanation.definitionFit: The calla, or arum lily, is a white-spathed plant commonly called a lily.

clue.text: 'Very holy' girl libertarian easily inveigles

indicators.note: to inveigle is to draw someone in, so the phrase holds a name within it

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A free-thinker easily lures in a saintly young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The name derives from Greek Ariadne, glossed as 'most holy', which explains the quoted phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariane is a female forename whose meaning is given as very holy.

clue.text: Position of European noble giving endless party in seaside resort

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so the final letter goes
in sets one word inside another

blocks.note: Margate is a seaside town in Kent
a rave is a big dance party

explanation.surface: A continental aristocrat throws a non-stop party at the English seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is a traditional English seaside resort in Kent, popular with Londoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A margravate is the territory or rank of a margrave, a German nobleman.

clue.text: Beneficiary, certainly, within price-earnings ratio

indicators.note: within places one word inside another

blocks.note: the P/E ratio is a stock-market measure
aye means yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A shareholder certainly gains from a good price-earnings ratio.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface hides the plain abbreviation P/E for price-earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is the one to whom money is paid, a recipient or beneficiary.

clue.text: Universal pub tipple — try imbibing one — undecided? (10, four words)

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one word takes another into its middle

blocks.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
a pint is the classic pub drink
to try a case in court is to hear it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drinker can't choose between the pub's universal pint and something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The I sits inside HEAR between the A and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan up in the air is unsettled, so the idiom means undecided.

clue.text: Pedlar, clumsy one, person with tent of skins

blocks.note: bod is informal for a person
a ger is a Mongolian felt or skin tent, a yurt

explanation.surface: A list of odd characters: a hawker, a klutz, a nomad in his hide tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part of the clue gives two senses of the answer at once; 'person with tent of skins' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists bodger both as a dialect word for a hawker and as a botcher who does clumsy work.

clue.text: Old park officer also pulled up medicinal plant

indicators.note: pulled up means drawn upward, and in a down answer that reads the word backwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a ranger patrols a park
too means also

explanation.surface: An old park keeper also uproots a herb used in medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled up' suits uprooting a plant, but it turns the last word around.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeroot is goldenseal, a North American herb whose root is used medicinally.

clue.text: Viscous liquid container ass dropped, aerated?

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so these letters leave the word

blocks.note: a glass holds a drink
taken as written, to be removed
airy means full of air

explanation.surface: A donkey knocks over a pot of thick fluid, which gets frothed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viscous liquid' reads as one phrase, but only 'Viscous' is the definition; 'liquid container' is the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Glair is egg white, so glairy describes something slimy and thick like it.

clue.text: Motorway group, not united in revealing distance travelled

indicators.note: 'not united' asks for the letter standing for united to be left out

blocks.note: the M1, written MI in crosswords, is Britain's first long motorway
a league is a grouping of teams or nations
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A motorway pressure group reveals how far it has driven without unity.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mileage is the number of miles covered, a measure of distance travelled.

clue.text: Dorothy, perhaps, joins mum and Albert early in the day

blocks.note: ma is mother
Dorothy Tutin was a British stage and film actress
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: Dorothy meets up with her mother and Albert first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dorothy, perhaps' asks for a surname: Dame Dorothy Tutin, a British actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Matutinal means of or occurring in the morning, from Latin matutinus.

clue.text: It was fragile and it's broken

definitions.text: It was fragile and it's broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A delicate object that has now been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of 'It' and 'and' are broken up; 'was' signals an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Daint is an archaic form of dainty, meaning delicate, so in the old language a daint thing was frail.

clue.text: Knight consumed by passion, touching (4, two words)

indicators.note: being consumed by something means being swallowed into it

blocks.note: ire is anger, a fierce passion
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight overwhelmed by a moving, touching emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' looks like 'emotionally moving' but means 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is Latin for 'in the matter of', a formal way of saying concerning or about.

clue.text: Against embarking on 'Donna' ('mobile') at a measured pace?

indicators.note: mobile means movable, so the name's letters are free to move about
to embark on is to go aboard, so one word climbs inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
anti means against

explanation.surface: An objection to 'La donna è mobile', Verdi's aria, played at a steady tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'La donna è mobile' is the famous aria from Rigoletto, which makes 'mobile' look like part of a title rather than a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking, slightly quicker than andante, a moderate walking speed.

clue.text: Marine mammals thrashing about in sea riot

indicators.note: thrashing about means flailing wildly, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Seals splashing wildly in a stormy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair picture of the answer itself thrashing in the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Otaries are eared seals, such as sea lions, which are marine mammals.

clue.text: Landed estate not once under ancient townships

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under something means coming below it, so this piece is written second

blocks.note: demes were the townships of ancient Attica
ne is an archaic word for not

explanation.surface: An old country estate lying below some ancient villages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'under' means placed after, so the archaic NE comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held by a lord for his own use, a manorial estate.

clue.text: Chump, male, modelling dress

blocks.note: a clot is a fool
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A dim male model showing off a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a noun after 'modelling', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone is to dress them.

clue.text: Foreign racing driver, fantastically 'vite'? Here's panegyric

indicators.note: fantastically means in a wild, unreal way, so the word's letters are recast

blocks.note: Niki Lauda was the Austrian Formula One champion
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribute to an overseas racer who is fantastically quick, 'vite' being French for fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Vite is French for quick, which suits the racing-driver picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Panegyric as an adjective means formally praising, and laudative means expressing praise.

clue.text: It's painful for viewers — and it's welcomed by Murdoch possibly

indicators.note: being welcomed by someone means being taken in, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: Iris Murdoch was the novelist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Murdoch's media empire welcomes something TV viewers find painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murdoch' suggests the media mogul Rupert; the Murdoch needed is the novelist Iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Iritis is inflammation of the iris, a painful condition of the eye, which viewers use to see.

clue.text: Lost seat? A disappointment

blocks.note: first meaning: an obsolete word for a saddle or seat, 'lost' marking it as gone from use
second meaning: a let-down or hoax

explanation.surface: An election defeat is a letdown for the candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost seat' reads as an election loss, but 'lost' flags a word no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the word as obsolete for a saddle or seat, and as a noun for a let-down or swindle.

clue.text: Cutting seconds and stuff

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
crap is slang for rubbish or stuff

explanation.surface: Seconds-quality offcuts and other bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like an adjective but is the noun, as in a newspaper cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a small piece clipped out, such as a cutting for a scrapbook.

clue.text: Doubt expressed in tremulous voice, one very lost inside

indicators.note: lost inside means gone from the middle, so interior letters are taken out

blocks.note: quavery means shaky, as a trembling voice is
a means one
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone voices uncertainty in a trembling tone, a little lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The A and V come out of the middle of QUAVERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A query is a question that voices doubt.

clue.text: Helping of lunch, a Ramadan tabu

indicators.note: a helping is a portion taken from a larger dish, so a run of letters is served from the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundaries of the three words

explanation.surface: Eating lunch during Ramadan is forbidden for the fasting Muslim.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene is apt: daytime eating in the fasting month is just what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Haram is the Arabic term for what Islamic law forbids, a religious taboo.

clue.text: Rough sketch of queen in emergency is scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is thrown away, so these letters are discarded
in places one set of letters inside another

blocks.note: a crisis is an emergency
taken as written, to be removed
o' is a shortened form of of, as in o'clock
Qu is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A hasty drawing of the monarch in a crisis gets binned.
explanation.walkthrough: One IS is struck from CRISIS and O' QU fills the gap; 'of' doubles as the link and as the shortened o'.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquis is a quick preliminary drawing, French for a rough outline.

clue.text: Composer: left fragments of Albumblätte and light opera

indicators.note: fragments are small broken-off bits, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A composer left behind scraps of album leaves and an operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: An Albumblatt is a short piano piece, an album leaf, fitting the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Lalo was a French composer, best known for the Symphonie espagnole.

clue.text: Reverse of clean: in other words, putrid

indicators.note: the reverse of something is it turned back to front

blocks.note: nett means clear of all deductions, clean
or introduces an alternative way of saying something

explanation.surface: The opposite of clean, put another way, is foul.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends 'reverse of clean' is the definition, and rotten is indeed the opposite of clean, which makes it a neat trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrid and rotten both describe decomposing, foul-smelling matter.

clue.text: Keeps watch once island is surrounded by returning ooze

indicators.note: being surrounded means having something wrapped all round it
returning means coming back, so the word runs from its end

blocks.note: sew is a dialect verb meaning to ooze or drain
an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: A sentry on a muddy island keeps watch.
explanation.walkthrough: AIT, a river islet as on the Thames, is a crossword staple; 'once' marks the answer as an archaic spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Waites is an old spelling of waits, from wait in its former sense of watching or guarding.

clue.text: Recalling demigod, the lady's one, pure, nursing heart of faith

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter is kept
nursing means holding close, so one word cradles another

blocks.note: her is the possessive for a woman
a means one
clean means pure
the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: Memories of a hero: the woman alone, chaste, keeping faith in her heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes between the E and the A of CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Heracleian means of or like Heracles, the Greek demigod, so it recalls him.

clue.text: Skin bearing feathers partly concealed round goose's rump

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the letters are spun into a new order
concealed means hidden inside, so a letter is tucked within the others

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the rump is the tail end, here the final letter of goose

explanation.surface: A bird's feathered skin half hides the goose's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' looks like an instruction to take part of a word, but it is the fodder; the E is concealed after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pteryla is one of the tracts of a bird's skin on which feathers grow, as distinct from bare patches.

clue.text: Digger who becomes more overbearing with British around

indicators.note: the answer is what remains once the British abbreviation that surrounds it is taken off

blocks.note: bossier means more domineering
Br is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: An Australian who grows bossier in British company.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: wrap BR round the answer and you get a word for more overbearing. A Digger is an Australian, originally a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Digger is slang for an Australian, and Ossie is a variant spelling of Aussie.
